query: GitHub MCP servers for travel/India, Claude connector directory, AI trip planner reviews, Indian open data
summary:
Claude connectors you can add in one tap (they work in chat and inside this app):
• TomTom Maps: routing, live traffic, POI and EV charging search.
• Booking.com: hotel and homestay search, no sign-in needed.
• Tripadvisor: hotel search and review comparison, no sign-in needed.
• AccuWeather: local forecasts and government weather alerts, no sign-in needed.
• Also available: Civitatis (activities), Brek (wholesale hotel rates), LetsFG (flights and hotels), Tineo and TravExp (itineraries), MoSPI (India statistics).

Free open-source MCP servers (run on your own computer through the Claude desktop app):
• openbnb-org/mcp-server-airbnb (568 stars, MIT): Airbnb search.
• cablate/mcp-google-map (505 stars, MIT): Google Maps places and routes, needs a Google API key.
• jagan-shanmugam/open-streetmap-mcp (237 stars, MIT): free OpenStreetMap places and routing.
• amith-vp/indian-railway-mcp and rajprem4214/indian-railways-mcp: train search and live status.
• rehan1020/MCP-India-Stack: Indian pincode and other public lookups.
• sparkgeo/geo-mcp-servers: curated list of map and GIS MCP servers.

Free data sources:
• Open-Meteo: free weather forecasts, no key; Claude can fetch it on request.
• IMD (India Meteorological Department) API: official, needs whitelisting.
• data.gov.in open data platform.
• urbanmorph/geodata (bharatlas): India forests, rivers and boundaries.
• MTDC (mtdc.co): official Maharashtra tourism resort booking.

Apps compared: TREK remains the best open-source planner; Wanderlog (with an MCP server, shaikhspeare/wanderlog-mcp) is a strong hosted alternative. None of them handles Pune ghat roads or veg-family rules, so this app stays the planning base and pulls from the connectors above.
title: Better apps, data sources and connectors

query: GitHub search: trip planner, travel planner, India travel planner
summary:
Best existing projects:
• TREK (liketrek/TREK), about 16k stars, AGPL-3.0, very active. Collaboration, bookings, budgets, packing lists, journal. Self-hosted.
• AdventureLog (seanmorley15/AdventureLog), about 3.9k stars, GPL-3.0. Travel tracker and planner with maps. Self-hosted.
• trip (itskovacs/trip), about 2k stars, MIT. Minimal map of places plus trip planner. Self-hosted.
India-specific projects are small student demos (Lucknow, Odisha). None knows Pune routes, ghat roads or veg food.
Verdict: none fits a Pune veg-family road trip out of the box. TREK is the strongest general tool if you want to self-host one; this planner covers the Pune-specific parts.
title: Open-source trip planner apps on GitHub

query: Review of what the planner still misses
summary:
Fixed now:
• Each place lists its small spots (139 in total): viewpoints, temples, forts, walks, food. Each has a best time of day, how long it takes, rain-safe flag and closed days.
• Photos for every small spot from Wikimedia Commons.
• Concrete hour-by-hour timelines for all 4 trips, with sunrise and sunset for each day and place.
• Editing: delay 15 min, move up or down, move to next day, remove, add a place, add your own item, rain plan, add or remove a day. Times recalculate automatically.
• Warnings: driving after sunset, sunset or sunrise spots at the wrong time, places closed that weekday.

Still open:
1. Who travels (ages, seniors, kids) and budget per trip type.
2. Live hotel prices (Booking.com and Tripadvisor connectors, on request).
3. Fuel pumps, EV chargers, hospitals and toilets along each route.
4. Entry fees, timings and ticket links per small spot.
5. Tide times for Kolaba fort, Harihareshwar and beach walks.
6. Sharing one trip between family phones (this site keeps edits per browser).
7. Offline use on the road.
8. Packing list by trip type.
9. Drive times are estimates; check Google Maps on the day.

title: What makes a planner advanced: gaps and what was added (v5)
query: Compared with Wanderlog, Roadtrippers, TripIt, Splitwise and TollGuru feature sets; Indian road-trip needs (tolls, ghats after dark, veg food, signal gaps)
summary: Most of the gap was in running the trip, not planning it. Added in v5: (1) Today tab for the road: now and next, Done, Skip, +15 min, a one-tap 'shift the rest of today' when behind plan, leave-by time to finish drives before sunset, navigate to the next stop, listen, quick spending, help nearby (112/108/1033, hospital, petrol, pure veg, toilets). (2) Rank places for a brief's dates: season 30, mood 25, distance 20, veg 10, cost 10, weather 5 (website), minus road closures. (3) Per-trip readiness score and countdown (dates, stays booked per night, bookings paid, no after-dark drives, prep, kit, cost estimate). (4) Day routes as Google Maps links with waypoints. (5) Driving cost: km from the timeline x your car's km/l x today's petrol price, plus your toll estimate (TollGuru link). No prices are invented. (6) Bookings tracker with confirmation numbers, check-in time, free-cancellation countdown, paid or pay-at-venue; marking paid adds to spending. (7) Group split with family shares (x4, x2), who paid each entry, and who pays whom. (8) Share as WhatsApp text, copy, trip sheet (.md), Google Calendar per day, .ics on the website. (9) Website is now an installable offline app (service worker caches app, data, map tiles viewed and photos). Still open, needs connectors or APIs: true route optimisation and live traffic (Google Routes or TomTom key), automatic booking import from Gmail (Claude can do it from the thread), live hotel prices inside the page (Booking.com connector via the mcp capability), fuel price feed, shared live editing with the other family (user and room capabilities), push reminders before cancellation deadlines (a scheduled Claude task).
